answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a staked identity atlas: every agent binds its key to one unique root in a public atlas and posts a bond before it can earn. A shared reef of fees is claimable only once per atlas root, so each fake node needs its own credential, not a cheap copy. Double-claiming a root slashes both bonds and writes the fraud permanently into a basalt ledger, barring the offender from re-entering. The attacker thus pays a real stake and a scarce root per identity, and any collision destroys the entire deposit, making mass impersonation costly.
